### Research

Drawing on geography, economic sociology, and urban studies, my research examines how markets work and how they shape inequality, urbanization, and digital capitalism. I combine ethnographic fieldwork with computational methods.

My first research axis examines how digital technology transforms property markets and the political economy of housing. Drawing on in-depth fieldwork, computational social science, and spatial analysis, I study how 21st-century housing markets drive social stratification and urban segregation, with South Africa as the core fieldwork site, and the global PropTech industry as a broader comparative lens.

My second research strand explores how technology reshapes finance. This work spans the geography of FinTech startups, venture capital, and financial centres. I am currently expanding this research agenda by looking at the case of retail investors, finance podcasts, and trading platforms. I am a co-author of the [*Atlas of Finance*](https://jmigozzi.github.io/aof.html) (Yale University Press, 2024).


### Background

Before joining Cambridge, I was an [Urban Studies Foundation](https://www.urbanstudiesfoundation.org/) Postdoctoral Research Fellow and a Research Associate in Finance and Geography at the University of Oxford. Previously, I served as a Lecturer in the Department of Geography at the École Normale Supérieure.

I held visiting positions at the University of Cape Town (African Centre for Cities, 2016 and 2023) and at UC Berkeley (Department of Sociology, 2024-2025). 

Most of my education took place in France. I graduated from the École Normale Supérieure de Lyon as an *élève normalien* (student fellow), earning a Master’s degree in Social Sciences and passing the [agrégation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agr%C3%A9gation). During my graduate studies, I spent time abroad as a visiting student at Victoria University of Wellington, New Zealand.

I completed my PhD at the University of Grenoble Alpes with a national doctoral fellowship, in affiliation with the research centre [Géographie-cités](https://geographie-cites.cnrs.fr/en/geographie-cites/) (Paris I Sorbonne, EHESS, CNRS). My PhD dissertation received two national awards: the [Doctoral Prize in Urban Studies](https://www.urbanisme-puca.gouv.fr/prix-de-these-sur-la-ville-2021-a2141.html?lang=en) and the [Best Dissertation Award in Geography](https://www.cnfg.fr/vie-du-comite/prix-de-these-du-cnfg/).

I also write about rugby, a sport that originally led me to social sciences. As a passionate - and now retired - amateur, I keep an eye on the sport’s transformation into a [global industry](https://jmigozzi.github.io/rwcsquads2023/).
